arabic text:
Ashur-e ka, suraj-e hai, kayamat ki gari hai. Bhayi ka, galaa kat ta, bahan-e
dekh rahi hai.
Maktal me kisi maa ki, sadaa gunj-e rahi hai. Aa e mere husain-e meri god-
e me aajaa. Aajaa, mere bache, meri aa gosh-e me aajaa.
english translation text:
The sun of Ashura has risen; it is the hour of Judgement. A sister watches
her brother's throat being cut.
A mother's voice echoes through the battlefield: Come, my Hussain, come into my lap.
Come, my child, come into my embrace.

arabic text: Mere liye ay laal-e tu asghar ki tarha he. Godi meri gehwaara hai bistar ki\ntarha hai. Is dhupe\nme daman mera chadar ki tarha hai.
english translation text: O my beloved, to me you are like Asghar. My lap\nis a cradle, and my embrace a bed. In this scorching sun,\nmy garment will become your covering.

arabic text: Me maa hu mera dil, nahi sin-e me sambhalta. Nazuk-e ye badan te ra ye\njalta huwa sehra. Or\nis me sitam ye, na ke tu rehgaya pyaasa
english translation text: I am your mother; my heart cannot remain steady within my chest. Your delicate body lies\nupon this burning desert, and beyond all this cruelty,\nyou have remained thirsty.

arabic text: Me god-e me laylu, tuje sine se lagaa lu. Sine pe sakina ki tarha tujko\nsulaalu. Sine me tere\ntir-e me palko se nikalu.
english translation text: Let me take you in my lap and hold you against my chest. Let me put you to sleep\nas you once put Sakina to sleep. I will remove the arrows\nfrom your chest with my eyelashes.

arabic text: Aakar mere zanu pe jo so jaa te the beta. Chuki ki mushakkat ke bhi pehlu,\nnahi badlaa. Ab\nkese tuje chor-e du maktal me akela
english translation text: My son, you once slept upon my knees. Even while grinding at the mill,\nI would never turn away from your side. How,\nthen, can I leave you alone in the battlefield?

arabic text: Teri bhi to awlad-e he tu bhi to padar hai. Awlad-e ka gham kya hai ye tujko\nbi khabar hai.\nGham bachche ka sehjaye ye kis maa ka jigar he.
english translation text: You too have children; you too are a father. You know\nwhat the grief of a child means. What mother's heart\ncould endure such sorrow?

arabic text: Tu let-e gaya thakke ke tu ise jalti zamin par. Ye kiska lahu tun-e malaa ruhe\nhasi par. Mat\nkhakh me pe so lal teri maa hai yahi par.
english translation text: You lie exhausted upon this burning earth. Whose blood have you smeared upon your radiant\nface? Do not sleep in the dust, my beloved—your mother\nis here beside you.

arabic text: Jo dil pe tere ghuzri me sub dekh-e rahi thi. Har lash-e uthane me tere sath-\ne gayi thi. Ab\nbat-e wo kehti tujo bach-e pan me kahi thi.
english translation text: Everything that passed over your heart, I witnessed. With every body you lifted,\nI walked beside you. Now I repeat to you the words\nI once spoke in your childhood.
